newsitem.title: GERMANY: Film about Larry Flynt wins Berlin Golden Bear.
newsitem.headline: Film about Larry Flynt wins Berlin Golden Bear.

text.p: "The People vs Larry Flynt", a film about the American pornography publishing king, won the top "Golden Bear" prize on Monday for best film at the 47th Berlin film festival.
Jury president Jack Lang told a news conference that the film, directed by Milos Forman, had won top honours.

The film depicts the tumultuous life of publisher Larry Flynt, a school drop-out who ran strip clubs in Ohio before launching his successful magazine Hustler in 1973. It won two Oscar nominations earlier this month.
The jury awarded Silver Bear prizes to Juliet Binoche for best actress for her performance in "The English Patient" and to Leonardo di Caprio for his role in "William Shakespeare's Romeo and Julia".
French star Binoche plays a French-Canadian nurse who helps a man suffering from amnesia in Minghella's film. Di Caprio plays the male lead in "Romeo and Julia".
"The English Patient", which has received 12 Academy Award nominations, and "The People vs Larry Flynt" were both expected to win awards in Berlin.
